newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says WTO ruling in India textile case favorable.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says WTO ruling in India textile case favorable.

text.p: A U.S. trade official on Monday took issue with interpretations of a World Trade Organization panel finding that suggested the panel found the U.S. violated trade rules in slapping import limits on woolen clothes from India.
"That is a misreading of the decision," said Jay Ziegler spokesman for the U.S. Trade Representative's Office.

"The panel ruled that the United States did meet the burden of proof that there was harm in the domestic marketplace," he said. The panel said that the criteria used by the United States to show harm to the domestic marketplace by the imports were valid, he said.
Trade sources in Geneva had said earlier on Monday that the panel found against the United States.

Ziegler said that the panel did say that the United States had an obligation in any future potential restraining actions to submit more detailed information to the Textile Monitoring Body about harm in the domestic marketplace.
"That is a very narrow view of the issues that were at stake here," Ziegler said.
The WTO dispute settlement panel backed an earlier decision by the Textile Monitoring Board that upheld the U.S. import restriction program, he said.
Indian officials had argued that the unilateral restriction ran against the 1994 world trade treaty and its Agreement on Textiles and Clothing.
A U.S. trade official said the WTO ruling would have no impact on the U.S. textile program and was generally supportive.
The United States voluntarily removed the import restrictions, which were introducted in April 1995, in December 1996 because the imports had declined.

The ruling had been communicated to the two countries in December. Those decisions are usually kept confidential for a period of time, giving parties in the case time to make further points. The textile ruling was distributed to other WTO members on Monday.
